parsed.why: Sodomy statute unenforced with no prosecutions; no trans-specific offence, no documented targeting, and a traditional third-gender role signals acceptance. Thin post-2015 data and latent statute keep it a step below full acceptance-plus-protections.

Decades of legality, marriage equality, administrative gender recognition, state-funded care, strong hate-crime penalties and active presidential support; no visitor-facing restriction documented. Prison-placement failures are resident-sphere; 2025 policy rollback is the main drag.

Article 521 directly criminalises trans-feminine presentation with six years; sodomy arrests, prosecutor-ordered anal examinations, a gathering ban and activist crackdown show state machinery aimed at gender-nonconforming people, though courts have partly pushed back.

Arrests based on clothing and appearance, standing extortion under Article 274, a 2023 morals-unit investigation, detentions past legal limits, trans women held in male prisons facing sexual violence, and near-universal societal hostility: pervasive state-tolerated targeting.

Centuries of legality, enforced hate-crime protection, no documented abuse or targeting, discrimination reported rare — offset by no gender-identity protection, no recognition, near-absent visibility and a conservative religious climate.
